correctness.rationale: A four-way exhaustive side-pattern decomposition yields exact conditional formulas F, J and epsilon-squared with correctly normalized weights. Independently integrated one-dimensional quadrature agrees with the closed expression over nine nontrivial aspect/threshold cases; three 1.6-million-triple Cartesian simulations across different aspect ratios and angles lie within five standard errors. Positivity and vanishing cubic term follow from an explicit log power series. In the dominant central distinct-side layer, Jacobian factorization gives an exact simplex-uniform law and a log variable whose density converges in L1; all excluded configurations have vanishing relative mass. Every quantifier and boundary is explicit. Finite checks are corroboration, not replacements for analytic proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The inspected boundary-polytope research proves large-sample expected-volume and face-count asymptotics; the inspected parallelogram-boundary theorem proves exact EXPECTED hull area and shape ordering, not tail stochastic domination. The original U-max results are for points on the unit circle and varying sample counts, with a smooth extremal configuration. None supplies a theorem strong enough to imply the exact near-maximal tail and marked law for three arclength-uniform boundary points on every parallelogram.

value.rationale: This answers a natural exact near-extremal distribution question for the canonical boundary-arclength measure, with an evaluated all-threshold positive kernel, an exact strict rhombus extremum among parallelograms, and a universal nonlogarithmic second coefficient (with missing cubic term). Continuous maximizing families create a logarithmic boundary singularity whose joint marks are explicitly Dirichlet and log-uniform. The statement is stronger than textbook expectation calculations and offers a precise benchmark for rare geometric network configurations.
